heading: INT. SALT MINE ELEVATOR CAGE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SALT MINE ELEVATOR CAGE - NIGHT
A steel cage the size of a confessional hangs in a shaft, two hundred meters of dark below its floor.
The walls sweat brine.
A single caged bulb swings, though the cage itself is still.
CASIMIR DRAGOMIR, 40s, mining engineer, hard hat cocked over one eye, grips the control lever with a white fist.
Across from him, wedged against the mesh, stands INSPECTOR LEILA FARHAT, 30s, in a borrowed orange jumpsuit two sizes too large, a laminated badge swinging at her sternum.
She keeps her eyes on the ceiling.
The cage shudders.
A shower of salt grit rains down on both of them.
You said it was a routine descent.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: It was routine until it stopped.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Then start it.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: I have pulled it eleven times.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Pull it twelve.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: He pulls.
The lever clacks.
Nothing.

There is a stone in the guide rail, or the cable has slipped a tooth, or the dispatcher has gone to his supper. I do not know which. I know only that I am forty-six years old and the sign at the top says six persons maximum and we are two and still we are not moving.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Do you want to hear what I wrote in my report on this shaft?
units.name: LEILA

units.text: No.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: That the guide rails were due for replacement in March.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: It is October.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Yes.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: Then you are a woman who knew.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: I am a woman who filed.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: A sound rolls up out of the dark below, a long metallic yawn, like a ship settling.
Both of them look down through the grated floor.
The bulb swings.
Neither speaks until it stops.
That is not the rail.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Then what?
units.name: LEILA

units.text: Somebody is in the shaft.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: A beam of white light cuts up through the grating from below.
It sweeps their boots, then their faces, then settles on Casimir's chest.
He raises a hand against it.

From the dark, a third person climbs into view along the guide rails, a dripping figure hand over hand: DOMINIK VESEL, 60s, a night-shift rigger in a rusted harness, a headlamp strapped to his forehead, a coil of rope slung across his shoulder.
He grips the cage floor and hangs there, grinning through salt-white stubble.
Forty minutes I have been under you, shouting.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: Dominik.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: You didn't hear.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: I did not.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Of course not. You never listen when the lever is in your hand.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: He hauls one leg onto the floor grate.
Leila steps back to give him room, though there is none.
Who is this?
units.name: LEILA

units.text: My rigger.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Madam, with respect, if you knew what I know about this cable you would not be standing so calmly.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: I am not calm.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: Then you are the first sensible one today.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: He swings the rope off his shoulder and clips it to a ring in the cage wall, then to his harness, then, without asking, to Leila's belt.
She looks down at the carabiner clicking shut against her hip.
What are you doing?
units.name: LEILA

units.text: Insurance.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: Dominik. Tell us.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Dominik wipes his face.
His grin goes.
The cable is fraying at the third splice. Not the first, the third. It will hold a minute, maybe two. Not more.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: You are certain?
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: I held it in my hand.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: The cage jerks.
A hard small drop, an inch, then it catches.
All three go rigid.
Move the lever.
units.name: LEILA

units.text: If I move it the splice may part.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: And if you don't?
units.name: LEILA

units.text: Then the splice may part anyway.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: Dominik laughs, one short bark that echoes in the shaft.
He claps Casimir on the shoulder.
There. A man who understands the odds.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: Casimir takes a long breath.
He sets his hand on the lever, and with the other hand he reaches out and grips Leila's wrist.
Hold the mesh. Both hands.
units.name: CASIMIR

units.text: She does.
He pulls the lever down.
The cage lurches, climbs a meter, a second meter, screaming against the rail, then stops again so hard that her hard hat clatters off and falls away into the dark.
They all listen to it fall.
It does not hit anything for a very long time.
That was a good hat.
units.name: DOMINIK

units.text: Above them, far up the shaft, a pinprick of daylight-colored lamp appears and begins to grow.
